selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

experiences.name: Explore Djemaa el-Fna Square
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at this UNESCO-listed square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and musicians perform as the sun sets. Sample street food like msemen flatbread, harira soup, and fresh-squeezed orange juice from the surrounding stalls.

experiences.name: Camel Trek and Overnight Desert Camp in the Sahara
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset and spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a sky full of stars. Enjoy a campfire dinner with tagine, mint tea, and live Gnawa music. Wake at dawn to watch the sunrise paint the dunes in shades of orange and red.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Guided Tour of the Medina and Historic Souks
experiences.description: Navigate the labyrinthine alleyways of Marrakech's ancient Medina with a knowledgeable local guide. Visit the Medersa Ben Youssef, the Saadian Tombs, and the Bahia Palace, then wind through the spice, leather, and textile souks. Learn about centuries of Moroccan craftsmanship and trade history.

experiences.name: Sandboarding on the Erg Chebbi Dunes
experiences.description: Strap on a sandboard and carve down the towering rust-red dunes of Erg Chebbi for an adrenaline-fueled desert adventure. Local guides provide boards and instruction, and the surrounding landscape offers dramatic photo opportunities. A perfect complement to the camel trek experience.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a riad kitchen and learn to prepare classic Moroccan dishes such as chicken tagine with preserved lemon, couscous with seven vegetables, and bastilla. Begin with a guided visit to the local market to select fresh spices and ingredients, gaining deep insight into Moroccan culinary culture.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the No. 19 public bus (approx. 20 MAD) or negotiate a petit taxi (approx. 70-100 MAD) to your accommodation. Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation stroll through the nearest medina streets to get your bearings and exchange currency at a local bureau de change for the best rates.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Djemaa el-Fna square at sunset to witness the magical transformation of the plaza — snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians fill the space. Grab a seat at one of the open-air food stalls in the square for an authentic and affordable Moroccan dinner. Try harira soup, kefta brochettes, and fresh-squeezed orange juice.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Quick bite at airport or a street-side café near the medina after check-in — msemen flatbread with honey and argan oil (15-25 MAD)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna night market food stalls — full meal of harira, kefta, bread, and fresh orange juice for approx. 60-80 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light due to afternoon arrival. Exchange cash to Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) upon arrival — ATMs at the airport are reliable. Avoid aggressive touts near the square; politely decline and keep walking. Budget tip: the No. 19 bus from the airport is a fraction of the taxi cost.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only for non-Muslims) — free and stunning at sunrise. Walk to the Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of the most beautifully ornate Islamic schools in North Africa (entry approx. 70 MAD). Explore its intricate tilework, carved stucco, and cedar wood ceilings. Nearby, visit the small but fascinating Marrakech Museum housed in the Dar Menebhi Palace (combined ticket available, approx. 50 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Lose yourself in the souks of the medina — the spice souk (Rahba Kedima), leather souk, and metalwork souk are all within walking distance. Practice your bargaining skills! Visit the Chouara-style dyers' souk to watch artisans at work. Head to the Saadian Tombs (entry approx. 70 MAD), a beautifully preserved royal necropolis dating to the 16th century. Walk to El Badi Palace ruins for sweeping views and fascinating history (entry approx. 70 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna for sunset. Climb to a rooftop café terrace overlooking the square for mint tea (Café de France or Café Argana area) — a pot of tea costs about 25-35 MAD. Dinner in a local restaurant just off the square in a side alley for a budget-friendly tagine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near the medina — café au lait, msemen, and amlou (almond-argan dip) for 20-30 MAD
meals.lunch: Street food in the souks — a bowl of bissara (fava bean soup) with bread and olive oil for 10-15 MAD, or a sandwich from a local snack stall for 20-30 MAD
meals.dinner: Local restaurant off Djemaa el-Fna — chicken or lamb tagine with bread and mint tea for 60-90 MAD per person. Look for restaurants with Moroccan clientele for best value.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the medina streets are cobblestone and uneven. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) out of respect for local culture. Keep a small amount of cash in an accessible pocket for small purchases. Budget for the day: approx. 250-350 MAD including entry fees, meals, and transport.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Majorelle Garden (entry 150 MAD including the Berber Museum inside) — arrive early to beat the crowds. The cobalt blue buildings and exotic plants are iconic. Just outside, the surrounding Hivernage neighborhood is pleasant to stroll. Alternatively, the Menara Gardens are free to enter and offer serene olive groves and an iconic pavilion reflecting in a large pool — a great budget alternative.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the historic Bahia Palace (entry approx. 70 MAD), a stunning 19th-century palace with lavish courtyards and painted ceilings. Walk through the Mellah's covered market and old synagogue area. Stop at a local hammam for a traditional Moroccan bath experience — public hammams cost as little as 15-20 MAD (bring your own kessa glove and black soap, available in the souks for 20-30 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Take an evening cooking class or simply enjoy a relaxed dinner. Visit the weekly local food market if timing aligns, or explore the Mouassine neighborhood for its quieter, more artisan-focused souks. End the evening with a walk along the lit-up ramparts of the medina walls.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your accommodation or a local patisserie — fresh msemen, honey, and coffee for 25-35 MAD
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from the Mellah market — fresh bread, olives, cheese, and seasonal fruit for 30-40 MAD total
meals.dinner: Try a local Moroccan restaurant in the Mouassine area — pastilla (sweet-savory pigeon or chicken pie) followed by couscous for approx. 70-100 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Book a shared hammam visit rather than a private spa to save significantly. The Majorelle Garden can be skipped if budget is very tight — the free Menara Gardens offer a similarly peaceful experience. Today is also a good day to book your Sahara desert excursion for Day 4-6 if not already arranged — look for group tours departing from Marrakech (3-day shared tours start from approx. 1,500-2,000 MAD per person).

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - 2027-03-18 (Journey to the Sahara - Dades Valley)
day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (6:00-7:00 AM) on a shared group minibus tour heading toward the Sahara via the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m). Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar — a breathtaking fortified village used as a backdrop in countless films including Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the kasbahs and enjoy views over the Ounila River valley. Entry to the ksar is free; a small tip to a local guide (20-30 MAD) is appreciated.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the journey through the Rose Valley and the dramatic Dadès Gorge. Stop at Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') for a brief visit to the Atlas Film Studios (entry approx. 50 MAD) or simply admire the Taourirt Kasbah from outside. Drive through the Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs — the landscape becomes increasingly dramatic and arid. Arrive at your overnight stop in the Dadès or Draa Valley area.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a budget guesthouse (auberge) in the Dadès Valley or Tinghir area. These simple but charming guesthouses typically cost 100-150 MAD per person for a dorm bed or 200-300 MAD for a private room. Enjoy a communal Berber dinner with fellow travelers around a shared table.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at accommodation before departure — bread, jam, argan oil, and coffee/tea (included or 20-30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop at a local restaurant near Aït Benhaddou — Berber omelette or tagine with bread for 40-60 MAD
meals.dinner: Communal dinner at the guesthouse — traditional Berber tagine, salads, and mint tea for approx. 80-100 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Book a shared group tour from Marrakech rather than a private tour to dramatically reduce costs — shared 3-day Sahara tours typically include transport, basic accommodation, and some meals for 1,500-2,000 MAD. The road over Tizi n'Tichka can be winding — take motion sickness tablets if needed. Bring a light jacket as mountain passes can be cool even in March.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and continue the journey toward Merzouga and the iconic Erg Chebbi dunes — the largest sand dunes in Morocco, reaching up to 150 meters high. Stop at the Todra Gorge (Gorges du Todra) en route — a spectacular narrow canyon with walls up to 300 meters high. Walk through the gorge floor (free, no entry fee) and enjoy the dramatic scale of the rock formations. This is a highlight of the entire trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Merzouga village by early afternoon. Check into a budget desert camp or guesthouse at the edge of the dunes (100-200 MAD per person for basic accommodation). Spend the afternoon at leisure — explore the village, watch local Gnawa musicians, or visit the small lake near Merzouga where migratory birds stop in spring. Optionally hire a local guide for a short dune walk (negotiate firmly, aim for 50-80 MAD for a 1-hour walk).
day_by_day.evening: The highlight of the entire trip: mount a camel at sunset for a 1-hour ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes to a traditional Berber desert camp (typically included in group tour packages, or approx. 200-300 MAD independently). Watch the sun set over an ocean of golden sand dunes — one of the most spectacular sights in Africa. Enjoy a Berber drum circle around the campfire under an extraordinary star-filled sky. Sleep in a traditional nomad tent.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at guesthouse — bread, honey, olive oil, and Moroccan mint tea (included in most guesthouses or 25-35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop near Todra Gorge — sandwich, fruit, and water for 30-40 MAD
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — lamb or vegetable tagine, Moroccan salads, and mint tea served under the stars (typically included in camp stay, or 80-120 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a headscarf or buff to protect against sand and wind in the dunes. Temperatures in the Sahara in March are very pleasant during the day (20-28°C) but can drop significantly at night (5-10°C) — bring a warm layer. Protect your phone and camera from sand. The camel ride is a must-do experience; prices are negotiable if booking independently. Stargazing at Erg Chebbi with zero light pollution is extraordinary — bring a star map app.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (around 5:30-6:00 AM) to climb the nearest high dune and watch the sunrise paint the Sahara in shades of gold, orange, and pink — a truly unforgettable experience. Take your time descending and enjoy a final Saharan breakfast at the camp. Pack up and begin the long return journey toward Marrakech via a different route through the Ziz Valley and the dramatic Ziz Gorges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the fortified city of Er Rachidia and the Ziz Valley — a lush palm oasis cutting through barren desert landscape. Continue through the Middle Atlas mountains, passing through cedar forests where Barbary macaque monkeys can sometimes be spotted roadside (do not feed them). Stop at the charming mountain town of Midelt for a late lunch break.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by late evening (approximately 20:00-21:00 depending on stops). Check back into your accommodation, shower off the desert dust, and enjoy a quiet final night in the medina. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs from the night market stalls near Djemaa el-Fna.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at the desert camp — Berber bread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea (included in camp stay)
meals.lunch: Stop in Midelt — a bowl of harira soup and fresh bread at a local café for 20-30 MAD, or a tagine for 50-70 MAD
meals.dinner: Back in Marrakech — a well-deserved sit-down dinner at a local restaurant in the medina. Try pastilla or mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) for 70-100 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: The return journey is long (approximately 9-10 hours with stops) — bring snacks, water, a book, or downloaded entertainment. The Ziz Valley route offers completely different scenery from the outward journey, making it worthwhile. Budget tip: if you feel unwell from the long drive, ginger candies or biscuits help with nausea on mountain roads.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning visiting any remaining Marrakech sights you missed earlier in the trip. Consider the Musée de la Femme (Women's Museum) for a unique cultural perspective (entry approx. 50 MAD), or revisit favorite spots in the medina. If you haven't yet, visit the Cyber Park Arsat Moulay Abdeslam — a free public garden with free Wi-Fi, perfect for uploading photos and relaxing. Do final souvenir shopping in the souks — best deals are on leather goods, argan oil products, spices, and hand-painted ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a final leisurely lunch in the medina. Pack your bags and check out of accommodation. If your flight is late, most guesthouses will hold luggage for free. Take a final walk around the Koutoubia Mosque gardens and along the ramparts. Head to the airport by petit taxi or bus — allow at least 1.5 hours before departure. The No. 19 bus runs regularly and costs only 20 MAD; a petit taxi should cost 70-100 MAD.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, history, desert adventure, and authentic Moroccan experiences — all achieved on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at a local café — café au lait, msemen with amlou, and fresh-squeezed orange juice for 25-35 MAD
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a rooftop restaurant near Djemaa el-Fna — a full Moroccan spread with tagine, salads, bread, and mint tea for 80-100 MAD. Splurge slightly as a trip send-off!
meals.dinner: Light snack at the airport or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Best budget souvenir buys: loose spice blends (ras el hanout, cumin) — 20-50 MAD per bag; small hand-painted ceramic dishes — 30-80 MAD; pure argan oil — 50-100 MAD for a small bottle (buy from a women's cooperative for fair trade guarantee). Always bargain in the souks — starting price is typically 2-3x the fair price. Tip: pay in MAD rather than euros to avoid unfavorable exchange rates offered by sellers.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort and check in. Freshen up and orient yourself with the hotel amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle introductory stroll through the nearby Gueliz (Ville Nouvelle) neighborhood. Browse the Majorelle Garden (Jardin Majorelle) — a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden co-restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the lush cacti, fountains, and the small Berber Museum inside.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Djemaa el-Fna square as the sun sets to witness the legendary transformation — snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls ignite the night. Soak in the atmosphere from a rooftop café terrace overlooking the square.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Café de France or a quick bite at a café near the airport/hotel during transfer
meals.dinner: Dinner at one of the open-air food stalls at Djemaa el-Fna — try harira soup, merguez sausages, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (budget-friendly, ~150–200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a bureau de change in Gueliz. Dress modestly when exploring the medina. Keep small bills handy for tips at Djemaa el-Fna stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Deep dive into Marrakech's historic medina. Visit the magnificent Bahia Palace (9th-century Moroccan architecture with intricate tilework and carved cedar ceilings), then walk to the nearby Saadian Tombs — a 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring stunning marble and mosaic craftsmanship.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of the largest Islamic colleges in North Africa with breathtaking Andalusian-Moroccan architecture. Afterward, get wonderfully lost in the souks — navigate the labyrinthine lanes of the spice souk, leather souk, and lamp souk. Practice your bargaining skills for souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Moroccan dinner with live Gnawa or Andalusian music at a mid-range riad restaurant in the medina. Enjoy a full set menu with pastilla, tagine, and bastilla au lait for dessert.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a local café — msemen (Moroccan flatbread), amlou (argan oil and almond paste), and mint tea (~60–80 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices near the spice souk — rooftop terrace, fresh salads, and Moroccan wraps (~120–160 MAD)
meals.dinner: Riad Yima or similar mid-range riad restaurant — set Moroccan menu (~250–350 MAD per person including tea)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a licensed guide for the morning medina tour (~300–400 MAD for 3 hours) to avoid unofficial guides. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the medina streets are uneven cobblestone.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Atlas Mountains — depart early by shared grand taxi or organized day tour to the Ourika Valley (~30 km from Marrakech). Hike through terraced Berber villages, fragrant argan and olive groves, and follow the Ourika River upstream toward seasonal waterfalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Berber family's home for an authentic mint tea ceremony and learn about traditional Berber culture and argan oil production. Continue the hike toward the Setti Fatma waterfalls (approximately 45-minute moderate hike). Swim in the cool natural pools if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech by late afternoon. Unwind with a traditional hammam experience at a mid-range local hammam near the medina (not a tourist spa — the real thing). Enjoy a kessa scrub and ghassoul clay treatment.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab msemen and coffee at a local bakery before departure
meals.lunch: Riverside tagine lunch at a local Berber restaurant in Setti Fatma village — trout tagine is a regional specialty (~150–200 MAD)
meals.dinner: Light dinner at a neighborhood Moroccan restaurant near the hotel — couscous Friday special or brochettes with khobz bread (~150–200 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Bring layers — the Atlas Mountains can be cool even in March. Wear sturdy shoes for the waterfall hike. Book the hammam in advance; budget ~150–250 MAD for the full traditional experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (6:00–7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via a private or shared transfer along the spectacular Draa Valley route over the High Atlas Mountains. Pass through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260 m elevation) with sweeping mountain panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa' — to visit the Kasbah Taourirt, a stunning earthen fortress, and the nearby Atlas Film Studios where films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones were filmed. Continue driving through the Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs toward Zagora or Merzouga (depending on final Sahara camp destination).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara Desert by late afternoon. Mount dromedary camels for a 45-minute sunset camel trek into the Erg Chebbi or Erg Chigaga dunes. Arrive at your desert camp as the sky turns amber and violet. Watch the sunset from the top of a golden sand dune.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — pack snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Ouarzazate at a local restaurant — Berber pizza (madfouna) or lamb tagine (~150–200 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp under a sky full of stars — harira, tagine, Berber bread, and mint tea included in most camp packages

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Marrakech to Merzouga is approximately 8–9 hours. Consider a private transfer (~800–1,200 MAD per person) for comfort. Pack a headscarf/shemagh for the camel ride — desert winds carry fine sand.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (5:30 AM) and climb the nearest large dune to watch the Saharan sunrise — one of the most spectacular natural experiences in Morocco. The silence and the shifting colors of the dunes from deep purple to burning orange are unforgettable. Return to camp for a Berber breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the desert on foot or by 4x4 — visit a nomadic Berber family's tent for tea, learn about desert survival traditions, and explore the fossilized marine beds around Erfoud (the area was once an ancient sea). Optionally try sandboarding on the dunes.
day_by_day.evening: As the heat of the day fades, take another short camel or walk through the dunes. Gather around the campfire as night falls — your Berber hosts will play traditional Gnawa drums and guembri music under an extraordinary star-filled sky. Stargaze in one of the lowest light-pollution zones in the world.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Berber camp breakfast — msemen, honey, argan oil, hard-boiled eggs, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at the camp or a nearby desert auberge — Berber omelette, salads, and tagine (~included in most camp packages or ~150 MAD separately)
meals.dinner: Communal campfire dinner at the desert camp — slow-cooked lamb or chicken tagine with preserved lemon, followed by Moroccan pastries

day_by_day.notes: Temperatures in the Sahara in March: warm days (~25–28°C) and cool nights (~10–12°C). Bring a warm layer for the sunrise and evening. Protect your camera and phone from fine sand. Tipping your camel guide (~50–100 MAD) is appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: After a final camp breakfast, depart the Sahara and begin the return journey toward Marrakech via the northern route through the Ziz Valley and Todra Gorge. Stop at the spectacular Todra Gorge — towering 300-meter-high canyon walls with a crystal-clear river running through. Short walk through the gorge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Dades Valley (Valley of Roses — rose harvest season begins in late March/April). Visit the Aït Benhaddou UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) — one of the most photographed earthen architecture sites in the world, appearing in Lawrence of Arabia, The Mummy, and Gladiator. Walk through the ancient village with a local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by evening (approximately 7:00–8:00 PM depending on stops). Check back into the hotel. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the Gueliz neighborhood — the modern, European-influenced quarter with wine bars, contemporary Moroccan restaurants, and art galleries.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Tinghir near Todra Gorge — fresh trout from the river, salad, and Berber bread at a local riverside restaurant (~150–180 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a contemporary Moroccan restaurant in Gueliz — try Le Jardin or a similar mid-range spot with modern Moroccan fusion cuisine (~250–300 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The return drive via Todra and Dades is approximately 8–9 hours with stops. An early departure from the desert camp (7:00 AM) is recommended. Aït Benhaddou entry fee is approximately 10 MAD; a local guide costs ~100–150 MAD.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the El Badi Palace ruins, a 16th-century palace once described as one of the wonders of the world, now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on the ramparts. Explore the attached Museum of Photography and Visual Arts if interested.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks — pick up quality Moroccan leather goods, hand-painted ceramics, argan oil products, and saffron from the spice market. Visit the Ensemble Artisanal (government-fixed prices, no bargaining needed) for quality guaranteed crafts. Return to the hotel, pack, and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the medina — splurge slightly on your last night with a full traditional Moroccan feast: pastilla au pigeon, lamb mechoui, and chebakia (honey sesame cookies) with mint tea. Depart for the airport or extend your stay.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — enjoy the full spread on your last morning
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a medina café or food stall near the souks — Moroccan sandwich (kefta in khobz) and fresh orange juice (~60–80 MAD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Nomad Restaurant or La Maison Arabe — mid-range splurge (~300–400 MAD per person for a full Moroccan set menu with drinks)

day_by_day.notes: Marrakech Menara Airport is approximately 15–20 minutes from the medina by taxi (~70–100 MAD). Allow 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Declare any argan oil quantities over 1L at customs. Keep a small amount of MAD for airport tips and last purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in Marrakech. Upon arrival, enjoy a traditional Moroccan welcome with mint tea and rose water. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll through the resort gardens. If energy permits, explore the immediate surroundings of the Medina's southern quarter at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle introduction to Marrakech with a private guided walk through the illuminated Djemaa el-Fna square at dusk – witness fire eaters, musicians, and storytellers as the square comes alive. Return to the resort for a relaxed first evening.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Light welcome mezze platter and fresh juices served at the resort upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Maison Arabe or Dar Yacout – one of Marrakech's most celebrated riad restaurants. Enjoy a multi-course traditional Moroccan feast of bastilla, lamb tagine, and couscous in a candlelit courtyard setting with live Gnawa music.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Ask the concierge to brief you on the week's itinerary and confirm all bookings.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the UNESCO-listed Marrakech Medina. Visit the stunning Bahia Palace with its intricate zellij tilework and carved cedarwood ceilings, followed by the haunting ruins of the El Badi Palace, once adorned with gold and onyx. Explore at a leisurely premium pace with skip-the-line access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Saadian Tombs, one of Morocco's most exquisite historic sites. Afterward, immerse yourself in the souks with a private expert guide – explore the spice market, leather tanneries (Chouara), and artisan workshops. Enjoy a bespoke shopping experience with a personal stylist guide to select authentic Moroccan crafts, ceramics, and textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on a rooftop terrace overlooking the Koutoubia Mosque and the Medina skyline. Followed by an exclusive private cooking class at a luxury riad, learning to prepare traditional Moroccan dishes with a master chef.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Moroccan breakfast at the resort – msemen flatbreads, amlou (almond-argan dip), fresh orange juice, and pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant – contemporary Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views over the souks. Try the lamb merguez and harira soup.
meals.dinner: Private dining experience at the riad following the cooking class – enjoy the dishes you prepared, paired with Moroccan wines from the Meknes region.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina. Dress modestly when visiting religious and historic sites. Bargaining is expected in the souks – your guide will assist.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the breathtaking Majorelle Garden, designed by Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Explore the cobalt-blue villa, exotic cacti, and the Berber Museum within the grounds. Follow with a visit to the YSL Museum next door for a world-class fashion and art experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a traditional royal hammam experience at a luxury spa (such as Royal Mansour Spa or Es Saadi Spa) – enjoy a full black soap scrub, ghassoul clay mask, argan oil massage, and relaxation in ornate marble steam rooms. This is an unmissable Moroccan wellness ritual.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private performance of Moroccan music and Andalusian classical music (Malhoun) arranged exclusively at a historic riad. Then enjoy a sunset dinner at a fine-dining rooftop restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort with a selection of Moroccan and continental options
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café du Livre or Dar Cherifa cultural café – avocado toasts, Moroccan salads, and fresh pressed juices in a tranquil literary setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Salama or Dar Moha – modern Moroccan haute cuisine in an elegant setting. Try the pigeon pastilla and slow-cooked mechoui lamb.

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam session well in advance. The Majorelle Garden can be busy – arrive early for a more serene experience. The YSL Museum requires timed entry tickets.

day_by_day.morning: Private 4x4 excursion into the High Atlas Mountains. Visit the Ourika Valley and the Berber village of Setti Fatma. Trek through walnut and almond groves alongside the Ourika River, with a knowledgeable local guide explaining Berber culture, mountain ecology, and traditional village life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Ait Benhaddou Kasbah (UNESCO World Heritage Site) – one of the world's most spectacular earthen clay architecture sites and a famous film location (Game of Thrones, Gladiator). Enjoy a private guided exploration with a historian. Optionally, cross the river on stepping stones to explore the living village.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech by private vehicle. Enjoy a relaxing evening at the resort with an in-room spa treatment or a private pool session before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional Berber lunch at a local family home in the Atlas Mountains – freshly baked bread, olive oil, honey, tagine, and mint tea (pre-arranged through the concierge)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant or at Comptoir Darna – a vibrant Marrakech institution with belly dancing performances, cocktails, and refined Moroccan-French cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (around 8:00 AM) to maximize time in the mountains. Bring layers – temperatures in the Atlas can be cooler than Marrakech. This is a long day; comfortable footwear is essential.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 – March 19, 2027 (Journey to the Sahara – Merzouga)
day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Marrakech via private luxury 4x4 vehicle with a professional driver-guide. Drive through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m altitude) with breathtaking panoramic views of the High Atlas. Stop at a Berber cooperative to see traditional carpet weaving and purchase artisan goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley – a stunning landscape of date palm oases, ancient kasbahs, and red rock formations. Stop at Tinghir and the spectacular Todra Gorge – towering 300-meter limestone canyon walls. Short walk through the gorge with a guide.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the Sahara Desert near Merzouga. Check in to a luxury desert camp or boutique desert lodge (such as Scarabeo Camp or Erg Chebbi Lodge). As the sun sets, mount camels for a guided sunset camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes – one of Morocco's most iconic experiences.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch in a scenic oasis location, prepared by the resort and served by your private guide
meals.dinner: Exclusive private dinner under the stars in the Sahara Desert – a candlelit setup among the dunes with traditional Moroccan dishes, Berber musicians playing around a campfire, and a billion-star sky above.

day_by_day.notes: This is a full travel day (approximately 8–9 hours driving). Ensure the vehicle has climate control and comfortable seating. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a light scarf for the desert. The camel trek is approximately 45–60 minutes each way.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a private sunrise hot-air balloon ride over the Erg Chebbi dunes – one of the most spectacular views in all of Morocco. Watch the golden light slowly illuminate the vast sea of sand from above. Upon landing, enjoy a champagne breakfast in the desert.
day_by_day.afternoon: Adrenaline adventure in the dunes – choose from sandboarding down the tallest dunes, a thrilling quad bike excursion across the desert landscape, or a guided 4x4 dune-bashing experience. Visit a traditional nomadic Berber family encampment to learn about desert life, share tea, and hear stories passed down through generations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the luxury camp for a private rooftop stargazing session with a telescope and an astronomer guide – the Sahara's zero light pollution makes it one of the world's premier stargazing destinations. Unwind with a traditional hammam in the camp's private spa tent.

meals.breakfast: Champagne and gourmet breakfast served in the desert following the hot-air balloon landing
meals.lunch: Lunch at the luxury desert camp – fresh salads, grilled meats, and traditional Moroccan pastries served in a shaded Berber tent
meals.dinner: Private gourmet dinner at the camp with a specially curated menu of Moroccan and international dishes, fine wines, and live Gnawa music by the fire.

day_by_day.notes: The hot-air balloon must be booked well in advance and is weather dependent. Bring warm layers for the pre-dawn balloon ride – desert nights and early mornings can be cold in March. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk in the dunes before breakfast. Check out from the desert camp and begin the scenic return journey to Marrakech by private 4x4. Stop at the ancient Ksar of Aït-Ben-Haddou for a second, more leisurely exploration or visit the rose-growing region of Kelaat M'Gouna (Valley of the Roses) if timing allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by mid-afternoon. Use the remaining time for last-minute shopping in the souks for premium Moroccan argan oil products, leather goods, and artisan jewelry. Alternatively, enjoy a final relaxation session at the resort's pool or spa.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at one of Marrakech's most prestigious establishments – La Mamounia's Le Français or Le Marocain restaurant, set within the legendary La Mamounia Palace hotel. Toast to an extraordinary Moroccan journey with fine Champagne and an exquisite tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Final Sahara breakfast at the desert camp – traditional Berber bread, honey, argan oil, eggs, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch on the road – stop at a highly rated local restaurant in Ouarzazate for a fresh Moroccan spread
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner at La Mamounia – a legendary Marrakech institution frequented by royalty and world leaders. Multi-course tasting menu with Moroccan and French influences, fine wine pairing, and live traditional music.

day_by_day.notes: Allow sufficient time to reach the airport for your departure flight. Ensure all purchases are properly packaged for travel. Tip your guides, drivers, and camp staff generously – they are the heart of the experience. A standard luxury tip is 10–15% of service costs.
